name: JS1/legal-case-tracker

summary: In-memory Express+React case tracker. Astra fixed a real latent bug (setStatus delegated to update(), so every status call wrote an 'updated' history row and bumped updatedAt), added id tie-break sorting, page clamping and runtime body validation, and made the app exportable so 3 real HTTP tests can assert stored state. Verification is fully honest (logs show 3/3 pass, browser check present, all 19 file hashes match). Weakened by templated course furniture and a fractional-cent claim the code does not implement.

name: JS1/subscription-billing
top_fix: Choose one of subscription-billing/field-service/research-studies for the path and rewrite or drop the other two (02-CONCEPTS.md differs by 2 of 45 lines between them); then implement or delete the false 'fractional cent is rejected' claim, which is worst here because this is the billing app.
summary: Strongest JS/TS+PostgreSQL CRUD lesson after warehouse-ledger: list endpoint now counts and pages inside one REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY transaction with an id ASC tie-break and clamped page; PATCH /status takes SELECT ... FOR UPDATE and no-ops on an unchanged status; asyncRoute forwards rejected promises; a real seed bug (due_date vs "dueDate" in schema.sql) was fixed. The 4th test installs a failing trigger to prove the status update rolls back. Course prose is accurate on line refs but is a noun-swap of two siblings.

name: JS1/research-studies
top_fix: Drop from the path as a duplicate (02-CONCEPTS.md differs by 2 of 45 lines from field-service), and fix 01-CODEBASE-MAP.md:11 which calls the field a 'review date' when the code and JSON use dueDate/due_date everywhere (grep for reviewDate returns nothing).
summary: Third clone of the JS1 PostgreSQL trio, applied to /api/studies. The change is good - repeatable-read count+page, FOR UPDATE idempotent status, asyncRoute - and its one genuinely instructive detail is a real calendar-date validator (regex + ISO round-trip, rejecting 2027-02-29) paired with pg.types.setTypeParser(1082) so DATE values do not shift by timezone. Four honest tests, all evidence matches. But the course duplicates its siblings, names a 'review date' field that does not exist, and repeats the false fractional-cent claim.

name: JS1/warehouse-ledger
top_fix: Rewrite 07-TRACE-LAB.md's six 'Boundary' sections, which repeat one identical paragraph and all point at server/src/index.ts and lockProduct (including the two boundaries that describe client/src/App.tsx), so each names its real code; also delete the ~400 words duplicated verbatim from 02-CONCEPTS.md.
summary: Best project in the batch. Astra closed a real oversell race: every movement and transfer now takes SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the product row before computing SUM(delta), with an in-code comment explaining that locking the product (not the warehouse) also prevents deadlock between opposite transfers. Validation went from Math.trunc(Number(x)) coercion to Number.isInteger rejection bounded to int4, plus UUID and reason checks. Three tests prove it: two simultaneous -30 issues against 40 on hand return [201,400] with a final balance of exactly 10, and an injected trigger on the credit leg proves the transfer debit rolls back. Concepts chapter is written for this domain, not assembled from a template.

name: JS1/secure-notes
top_fix: Add session expiry - store {userId, expiresAt} in the tokens map in server/server.js, reject and delete expired tokens in requireAuth with the same 401, and add a test that a previously valid token 401s after the TTL. It is the missing half of this auth lesson and the course lists it only as future work.
summary: The batch's dedicated authentication-vs-authorization lesson, and it teaches the part juniors get wrong: notes are found by (id, ownerId) and another user's note returns the same 404 as a missing one, so existence does not leak. Astra hardened the credential path so a JSON object or array can no longer reach scryptSync, made email normalization symmetric across register and login (tested via a mixed-case login), bounded title and body, and added the missing owner-scoped GET /api/notes/:id. Caveats: ownership checks and logout revocation already existed (the Scope section implies otherwise), sessions never expire, and hashing is synchronous.

name: JS1/live-chat
top_fix: Decouple the two tests - test 2 opens ws://.../?room=study and depends on test 1 having created that room, so it cannot run alone; create the fixture in before() in test/chat.test.ts. Then teach LISTEN/NOTIFY properly in 02-CONCEPTS.md by showing the notify_new_message trigger at server/db/schema.sql:29-44, which the course never displays.
summary: Chat app over Express + ws + PostgreSQL LISTEN/NOTIFY. Astra replaced module-scope side effects (the backup had a bare server.listen at import, so importing the app bound a port and leaked a reconnect timer) with explicit startRuntime/stopRuntime, made malformed frames non-fatal (maxPayload 16384, per-event shape guards, connectSocket with a catch that closes 1011), and turned a silent slug coercion ('bad slug' became the different room 'bad-slug') into a 400 rejection. The integration test opens a real socket, throws three malformed frames at it, then proves a valid message both broadcasts and persists. Least CRUD-shaped and hardest project in the batch; only 2 tests and they are order-coupled.

name: newcodexJS/07-blog-platform
top_fix: Rewrite 07-TRACE-LAB.md's six 'Boundary' sections (one identical paragraph repeated six times, all pointing at services/service.ts and parsePayload) to name the real code at each step, and add a client test suite covering the stale-search sequence guard and double-submit guard at client/src/App.tsx:28-29, which the course advertises but nothing tests.
summary: Clearest CRUD-semantics lesson in the batch: create vs partial-update types, omitted vs explicitly-empty fields, JSONB is not a text array, and a delete of an already-deleted row should be 404. Astra replaced a field-allowlist with zod create/partial schemas, fixed a genuinely broken search (whereRaw CAST(posts AS TEXT) ILIKE matched ids and timestamps), made tag serialization explicit in both model and seed, added stable created_at desc/id asc ordering, and hardened the React form. Four tests run through real migrations against a real schema; all eight VERIFICATION rows are backed by checks.json logs, and the evidence even preserves Astra's own earlier failing runs. Dependencies are pinned here, unlike the JS1 projects.

name: newcodexJS/08-kanban-board
top_fix: Drop as a duplicate of 07-blog-platform (02-CONCEPTS.md differs by 1 line out of 45), or make it earn its name: add a position column plus a PATCH /api/cards/:id/move endpoint that computes a midpoint inside a transaction, and constrain the currently free-text lane to an enum. The seed even advertises 'Fractional ordering' as card text for a feature the app does not have.
summary: Same good change as 07-blog-platform applied to a cards table: zod create/partial schemas, the CAST(cards AS TEXT) ILIKE row-literal search fixed to per-column orWhereILike, explicit JSONB tag serialization in model and seed, stable ordering, and 404s on update/delete of a missing row, with four honest tests against a real schema. But the course is a one-line noun-swap of 07, and it is a kanban board with no kanban: no position column, no board/list tables, no move endpoint, and lane is an unvalidated string(255). Also ships Astra's pipeline id as the root package name 'astra-crud-workspace-59'.

name: newcodexJS/09-job-application-tracker
top_fix: Fix 02-CONCEPTS.md:7, where the noun-swap broke a claim: it promises 'explicitly sending an empty role means clear it', but services/service.ts:6 declares role: z.string().trim().min(1).max(255), so PUT {role: ""} is a 400. A learner following the course's own predict-then-run instruction will get the wrong answer.
summary: Third clone of the newcodex trio, applied to an applications table. The server change is as good as 07's - zod schemas, the CAST(applications AS TEXT) ILIKE search bug fixed, explicit JSONB serialization, stable ordering, real 404s - and Astra did correctly re-noun the tests to company/role. But the course is a one-line noun-swap of 07-blog-platform, the swap introduced a factually wrong partial-update claim, and the domain is unmodelled: stage and status are both unconstrained string(255) with no transition rules, so the pipeline lesson a job tracker exists to teach is absent.
